topic: Revive stat_dp_cate_fiber_tmechanism_frontier with the occupancy-weighted full-class sparse-to-dense pure-DP pointwise-CATE frontier and the presolve capsule embedded in this queued entry.

open_problems.open_problem: Can occupancy-weighted second-order projection scores yield one pure-DP pointwise-CATE estimator over the full unknown-propensity Hölder class, uniformly from sparse through dense cell occupancy and without nuisance-sieve entropy?

source_refs.excerpt: with C' independent of every finite nuisance sieve, using the same sample size n
Dense occupancy and the full-class target-fiber lift remain open.
an occupancy-weighted treated--control estimator exploits nearly common cell effects

source_refs.claim: Derives the nonprivate Hölder-class pointwise-CATE minimax frontier and its nuisance-smoothness elbow.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: Provides Neyman-orthogonal finite-query and functional CATE releases under approximate DP, but no pure-DP minimax frontier.
source_refs.author: Maresa Schröder, Valentyn Melnychuk, Stefan Feuerriegel

source_refs.claim: Exhibits a pure-DP sparse-versus-dense histogram tension: sparse output pays a domain-size cost that compact dense representations can avoid.
source_refs.author: Victor Balcer, Salil Vadhan

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked mechanism extracts signal from exactly-two-record cells and proves its radius only when cell occupancy nv is bounded; its one-record convex-hull obstruction rules out returning to additive scores under unknown propensity. Once nv diverges, exactly-two events vanish even though dense cells contain many informative pairs, while an unnormalized all-pairs statistic has occupancy-dependent record influence. Sparse-histogram and private-CATE results do not jointly privatize causal counts, coupled nuisance-product scores, and target-fiber selection. The missing proof must construct capped or self-normalized projection scores that retain the coupled signal, have an all-neighbor sensitivity certificate, and satisfy the nuisance-independent weighted-shell bound for arbitrary least-favorable priors.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit occupancy-adaptive finite pure-ε-DP estimator and a uniform full-class absolute-risk theorem proving R_DP(n,ε) is asymptotically equivalent to max{R_NP(n),r_G(n,ε),r_F(n,ε)} across all nv regimes, with matching same-class converses and constants independent of nuisance-sieve size.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from a precisely parameterized pointwise-CATE model to competing smoothness regimes, sharp elbows, and an attaining construction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: pointwise CATE depends on coupled smooth nuisances -> nonprivate information changes across smoothness regimes -> pure privacy adds occupancy-dependent barriers -> a full-fiber projection mechanism must attain the combined frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the occupancy-weighted treated-control estimator and its conditioning-on-counts proof, replacing its global approximately homogeneous contrast by localized nuisance-product projections.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its construction already aggregates random cells across sparse and dense occupancy instead of discarding cells containing more than two records.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over local Hájek-projection thresholding and reweighting to bound the instance-dependent sensitivity of occupancy-varying pair scores before pure-DP selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The dense-cell privacy cost is governed by the first-order projections and record influence of the proposed second-order statistic.

method_exemplars.technique: Use clipped stable test scores and the private T-mechanism proof, replacing finite-cover counting by the banked scalar distance-shell functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest test-to-private-estimator conversion once occupancy-adaptive composite scores are available.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the full-fiber lift first be proved on an explicit finite-dimensional Hölder sieve using one-sensitive profiled pair scores whose weighted-shell functional remains uniformly bounded as nuisance dimension grows?

source_refs.excerpt: Turn the full-fiber handle into a finite-dimensional pilot theorem for a specified Hölder sieve
The bound is independent of |G_r| and of every nuisance-sieve cardinality.
singleton mixtures from separated target fibers can coincide

open_problems.why_unsolved: The rejected randomized-treatment angle obtains a shell bound because one pseudo-outcome annihilates the baseline nuisance codebook. With unknown propensity, separated target fibers can instead have identical one-record mixture laws, and the signed pair construction restores a margin only for a specially symmetric sign family. On a general finite Hölder sieve, the first missing step is to profile pair contrasts over nuisance coefficients while keeping neighboring-dataset sensitivity at one and showing that erroneous score mass in each scalar target shell does not grow with the number of nuisance profiles.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For a specified wavelet or spline sieve of dimension K, an explicit family of profiled pair scores Q_t with global sensitivity at most one and uniformly bounded weighted-shell functional at the CATE information radius, yielding an ε-DP estimator with O(r) risk and no log K term.

writing_exemplar.why: Frame the result as removal of the finite-cover factor on a sharply delimited structured model rather than as a generic improvement to private hypothesis selection.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: stable tests enable universal private estimation -> generic finite covers charge nuisance cardinality -> ordered CATE fibers possess second-order structure -> establish entropy cancellation on an auditable finite sieve

method_exemplars.technique: Retain clipped-score sensitivity and exponential selection while replacing the global cover union bound with direct distance-shell integration.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed theorem targets the precise logarithmic step in the closest general private T-mechanism.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt composite tests between metric balls and their T-estimator aggregation to nested scalar CATE fibers with profiled nuisance coefficients.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired score family is a private higher-order analogue of composite-ball testing rather than pointwise hypothesis selection.

method_exemplars.technique: Stabilize each profiled pair contrast through local Hájek-projection bounds before shell aggregation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The nuisance-profiled scores remain order-two statistics, so record influence is the first privacy proof obligation.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the matched pure-DP separation frontier of the smooth signed two-fiber CATE experiment as nv crosses from sparse to dense occupancy, and does its n-squared-times-ε privacy branch persist unchanged?

source_refs.excerpt: Dense occupancy is the next unresolved elbow.
Add a lower bound on the same signed family showing that the collision/n^2-epsilon branch is unavoidable
restricted to q<gamma and nv<=c_0, at the named coupled radius r_F

source_refs.claim: Develops central-DP Le Cam, Fano, and Assouad inequalities based on couplings and expected Hamming transport.
source_refs.author: Jayadev Acharya, Ziteng Sun, Huanyu Zhang

source_refs.claim: Shows that pure-DP mechanisms can require different representations and incur different costs in sparse and dense histogram regimes.
source_refs.author: Victor Balcer, Salil Vadhan

open_problems.why_unsolved: The proved signed-family test replaces random cell counts by the probability of exactly two observations and obtains its pair-information scale only under bounded nv. When nv diverges, exactly-two events disappear although many within-cell pairs remain, while the replacement sensitivity of an unnormalized all-pairs score grows with occupancy. Generic private testing lower bounds can convert a suitable coupling into a converse, but no published result supplies the causal signed-mixture coupling or matching occupancy-adaptive upper statistic. The existing calculation therefore neither proves persistence of r_F nor excludes a new dense-cell privacy radius.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A piecewise characterization of the minimax testing or absolute-risk radius in n, ε, v, k, a, and b, with an occupancy-adaptive pure-DP test and a matching coupling-based lower bound in both bounded-nv and diverging-nv regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its phase-transition presentation is the natural model for stating a sparse-to-dense occupancy frontier with explicit elbows.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: localized CATE information arrives through covariate neighborhoods -> pair signals reveal nuisance products -> observations per microcell change the usable pair geometry -> determine the exact private separation elbow

method_exemplars.technique: Apply local Hájek-projection stabilization to occupancy-varying pair kernels and prove privacy and concentration after thresholding influential records.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Dense occupancy changes the pair statistic precisely through its first-order projection and record influence.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct occupancy-indexed mixture couplings and translate their expected Hamming transport into pure-DP Le Cam lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A matched local frontier requires a private mixture converse for the same signed experiment rather than a regression surrogate.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse conditioning on multinomial cell occupancies and occupancy-weighted treated-control contributions to interpolate between empty, lightly occupied, and dense cells.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its collision estimator aggregates information without discarding cells once they contain more than two records.

open_problems.open_problem: Does the occupancy-normalized pure-DP pointwise-CATE frontier transfer from exact-uniform covariate design to a known density bounded above and below without an additional density-geometry or privacy-rate term?

source_refs.excerpt: Broaden the exact-uniform benchmark to a known density bounded above and below
The exact occupancy normalization and deterministic projection geometry require a known exact-uniform random design
test whether bounded known design densities admit an occupancy-normalized analogue

source_refs.claim: Obtains near-minimax heterogeneous-effect rates with explicit density-ratio dependence without requiring covariate densities bounded away from zero.
source_refs.author: Zijun Gao, Yanjun Han

source_refs.claim: Constructs pointwise private wavelet estimators with near-matching rates for nonparametric regression under heterogeneous privacy constraints.
source_refs.author: T. Tony Cai, Abhinav Chakraborty, Lasse Vuursteen

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact uniformity makes every microcell probability public and equal, gives a common binomial occupancy law, and turns local projection algebra into deterministic equal-volume identities. With a merely bounded known density, cell masses differ and a multivariate probability-integral transform can distort Hölder smoothness. The first proof step that changes is the normalization and sensitivity analysis of pair blocks: inverse cell masses can amplify a changed record, while unequal occupancies invalidate the common shell-concentration bound. Existing heterogeneous-effect and private-regression results handle aspects of design geometry but not this pure-DP coupled-nuisance projection mechanism.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A public transport or cell-mass-weighted pure-DP mechanism with the same pointwise-CATE risk frontier up to constants depending only on density bounds, or a counterexample and matching bounds proving an additional density-geometry term unavoidable.

writing_exemplar.why: Its distinction between bounded-density lower classes and stronger attainability conditions provides the right motivation for an honest design-transfer result.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: pointwise CATE theory is formulated under positive local design density -> exact uniformity makes private occupancy algebra tractable -> realistic designs have unequal local masses -> determine whether public reweighting preserves the sharp private frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt occupancy weighting under arbitrary category masses and its reciprocal-count analysis to local unequal-mass partitions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates that unequal occupancy can be handled without equal-cell assumptions for a related causal collision estimator.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over nearest-neighbor rejection and density-ratio bounds to isolate the statistical cost of unequal local treatment-control mass.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest nonprivate CATE analogue in which local design geometry is explicit rather than hidden behind uniformity.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse private pointwise wavelet localization and density-dependent bias-variance calibration for the ordinary-regression component.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest private pointwise benchmark against which any extra causal density-transfer cost can be separated.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one central pure-DP pointwise-CATE procedure adapt simultaneously to unknown CATE smoothness, nuisance smoothness, and local arm occupancy, and what adaptation penalty is unavoidable in each sparse-to-dense regime?

source_refs.claim: Establishes distinct global and pointwise costs of smoothness adaptation under federated DP and proposes a one-shot adaptive estimator.
source_refs.author: T. Tony Cai, Abhinav Chakraborty, Lasse Vuursteen

source_refs.claim: Uses a privacy-modified Goldenshluger-Lepski rule for adaptive pointwise density estimation under local DP and proves optimality up to logarithmic factors.
source_refs.author: Sandra Schluttenhofer, Jan Johannes

source_refs.claim: Provides a model-agnostic approximate-DP CATE framework but delegates tuning of nuisance and CATE learners to the chosen base methods.
source_refs.author: Maresa Schröder, Valentyn Melnychuk, Stefan Feuerriegel

source_refs.claim: Shows that the nonprivate pointwise-CATE rate changes at a nuisance-smoothness elbow.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

open_problems.why_unsolved: Private model selection itself accesses the data, while the optimal localization width depends on target smoothness, nuisance smoothness, and the unknown treated and control masses near the target point. Existing adaptive private pointwise results concern density estimation under local or federated privacy, not pure central privacy with orthogonal-score nuisance products. Existing private CATE frameworks delegate tuning to base learners. The concrete obstacle is to choose occupancy and resolution through one privacy-preserving release without spending privacy budget at every scale, while separating the classical pointwise adaptation cost from any new privacy-induced logarithm.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A single ε-DP multiscale CATE estimator with an oracle inequality over a union of Hölder target and nuisance classes and local-mass exponents, paired with a matching adaptive lower bound identifying the exact logarithmic or iterated-logarithmic penalty in every occupancy regime.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames private CATE as a reusable meta-learning problem, naturally motivating replacement of learner-specific tuning by a theoretically adaptive procedure.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: private CATE requires flexible nuisance and second-stage learners -> performance depends on unknown local complexity and support -> a deployable pure-DP method needs one-shot adaptation across smoothness and occupancy regimes

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the one-shot multiscale noise mechanism and adaptive lower-bound construction, replacing density coefficients by localized causal-score coefficients.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest private pointwise adaptation result and explicitly separates privacy-induced adaptation cost from the nonprivate penalty.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt privatized Goldenshluger-Lepski comparisons across projection resolutions to occupancy-stabilized CATE estimates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its bandwidth-selection proof is structurally analogous but must be rebuilt for pure central privacy and two nuisance-adjusted treatment arms.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the causal smoothness elbow and higher-order local-polynomial construction as the nonprivate oracle family over which the private selector adapts.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It specifies the distinct pointwise-CATE regimes the adaptive mechanism must attain.

literature_map:
Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024, Annals of Statistics) give the nonprivate Hölder pointwise-CATE minimax frontier, including a nuisance-smoothness elbow and a localized higher-order R-learner.
Kennedy (2023, Electronic Journal of Statistics) supplies the two-stage doubly robust oracle inequality that exposes the nuisance-product remainder.
Gao and Han (2020, NeurIPS) derive HTE rates with explicit covariate-geometry and density-ratio dependence without a global lower bound on design density.
Niu et al. (2022, CLeaR) provide a private CATE meta-algorithm based on sample splitting and report pronounced privacy-induced variance for multi-stage learners.
Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025, ICLR) give Neyman-orthogonal finite-query and functional CATE releases, but their Gaussian constructions are approximate-DP rather than pure-DP frontier results.
Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen (2024, arXiv:2406.06755) establish pointwise Besov regression rates under heterogeneous federated approximate-DP constraints, supplying the closest private projection-rate analogue.
Lalanne, Garivier, and Gribonval (2023, TMLR) show central privacy can create new nonparametric density-estimation regimes and that pure-DP projection estimators may require relaxation for optimality.
Acharya, Sun, and Zhang (2021, Algorithmic Learning Theory) provide coupling-based private Le Cam, Fano, and Assouad lower bounds.
Györfi and Kroll (2025, Statistica Sinica) remove a strong design-density assumption for rate-optimal locally private regression, but study integrated prediction risk rather than central-DP pointwise CATE.
Schluttenhofer and Johannes (2022, arXiv:2206.07663) develop privacy-modified Goldenshluger-Lepski adaptation for pointwise density estimation under local DP.
Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen (2025, arXiv:2512.14337) identify an additional pointwise adaptation cost under federated DP and introduce a one-shot multiscale mechanism.
Balcer and Vadhan (2018, ITCS) expose a pure-DP sparse-versus-dense histogram tension: sparse output pays a log-domain per-bin cost, whereas compact dense representation can avoid it.
Kerschbaum, Lee, and Wu (2026, PACMMOD) obtain optimal pure-DP sparse-histogram error using private item blankets, but only for count release rather than causal score ratios.
Armstrong and Kolesár (2020, Quantitative Economics), Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017, Journal of Applied Econometrics), and Drechsler et al. (2022, Journal of Survey Statistics and Methodology) provide adjacent honest-inference ingredients, while no located paper combines them for pure-DP pointwise CATE.
prior_proposal_map:

The final parent proves only a sparse-occupancy signed-family pair test; its README and honest-scope text explicitly leave dense occupancy, arbitrary nuisance priors, global target-fiber aggregation, and the full-class estimator open.
The load-bearing surviving OEQ is oeq:full-fiber-pair-lift, which asks for one-sensitive scores with a nuisance-independent weighted-shell functional at the combined R_NP, r_G, and r_F radius.

The rejected angle-0 archive additionally contains an unverified bounded-to-binary Bernoullization minimax-equivalence theorem and documents why one-record scores fail under unknown propensity.
Mined the earlier downgraded stat_dp_cate_uniform_design_nuisance_privacy_frontier/v1, whose exact occupancy normalization is restricted to known uniform design and whose symbolic minimax-to-private transfer remains open.
Mined accepted stat_discrete_ate_heterogeneity_frontier/v1 as the principal technique donor: its total occupancy-weighted treated-control estimator handles arbitrary cell masses and all occupancy levels, but is nonprivate and targets a global approximately homogeneous ATE.
The active stat_dp_cate_densecell_projection_frontier/v1 directory contained orchestration state and no prior proposal core or reviewer JSON at scan time.
